description: The clock is read once per STATEMENT: every row of one INSERT stores the same CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, two calls inside one statement are equal, and the session-zone temporal family agrees with itself. SYSDATE is the same instant rendered in UTC rather than the session zone, a stored instant does not move when re-read, two statements inside one transaction get SEPARATE instants (the pin is per statement, not per transaction), and the pinned instant is a real reading rather than a frozen constant. Converted from features/StatementClockTest; its the-pin-does-not-outlive-its-statement test stays in the trimmed Java class (StatementClock.isPinned() is a static engine API with no SQL surface). The transaction test burns a GENERATOR scan between its two INSERTs: the pin is per statement, but two statements issued back-to-back can land inside one clock reading, and the Java class only avoided that by the framework overhead between its calls.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE ticks(id INT, ts TIMESTAMP_NTZ)
INSERT INTO ticks SELECT 1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 5))

skip.reason: pins the engine branch (its session zone is UTC, so the lead is zero); against live the Java class asserted instead that the lead is a whole number of quarter-hours within +/-14h

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE spans(n INT, ts TIMESTAMP_NTZ)
SELECT (SELECT ts FROM spans WHERE n = 1) <> (SELECT ts FROM spans WHERE n = 2)
